title: Provision a GitHub OIDC role and a vault-held, push-scoped Docker Hub token for mongodb-mcp-server
description: In the AWS account that hosts the company's aws-secrets-manager backend (sdlc/policy.json secretsManagement.backend), do the following. (a) Create or reuse the IAM OIDC identity provider for token.actions.githubusercontent.com. (b) Create an IAM role whose trust policy requires aud=sts.amazonaws.com and sub=repo:OnFinance/mongodb-mcp-server:environment:Production. Its permission policy allows only secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on one secret. (c) In Docker Hub, mint an access token limited to Read & Write on the mongodb-mcp-server image repository, and store the username and token in that one Secrets Manager secret, with a 90-day rotation reminder or schedule matching secretsManagement.rotationDays. Do not delete or change the existing DOCKERHUB_USERNAME/DOCKERHUB_PASSWORD GitHub secrets yet; they are the rollback path until task 3. No deployment window or change freeze applies (policy defines none).
acceptanceCriteria: The IAM role trust policy exported as JSON names the token.actions.githubusercontent.com federated principal, with StringEquals conditions aud=sts.amazonaws.com and sub=repo:OnFinance/mongodb-mcp-server:environment:Production, and no wildcard sub
The role's only permission is secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the single Docker Hub token secret ARN (IAM policy JSON attached as evidence)
The Secrets Manager secret's description output shows a rotation schedule or tagged next-rotation date no more than 90 days away
The Docker Hub token settings page (screenshot or export attached) shows the new token scoped to the mongodb-mcp-server repository with no access to other repositories or organisation admin

verificationMethod.description: The CISO reviews the attached IAM trust and permission policy JSON, the Secrets Manager describe-secret output and the Docker Hub token scope screenshot. Expected: the trust is limited to the repo and the Production environment, read is limited to one secret, rotation is 90 days or less, and the token is push-scoped to one repository.

rootCause.description: OIDC federation was set up only for the MCP Registry (mcp-publish.yml uses id-token: write). No federated role or vault-held registry token was ever created for Docker Hub, so the publish job fell back to a static username/password stored as GitHub secrets.
